This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Sri. C.Mogilappa caused in a Road Traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
On 26.08.2013 at about 3.00 p.m, Sri. Mogilappa was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ-4070 slowly and cautiously on the extreme left side of the road and when he reached near Gundugallu cross, on Punganur- Appinapalle Road,

Due to impact C. Mogilappa fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Punganur Government Hospital for treatment but due to severe injury succumbed to the injuries in the said hospital.
After Postmortem dead body of deceased was handed over to the petitioners.

4. After service of summons, the Respondent No.2 remained absent and he has been placed exparte.

The Respondent No.1/Insurance Company has appeared before this tribunal and filed written statement.
5.

The 1st respondent has admitted that, it is the insurer of offending Tractor and Trailor and contending that, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, provisions of M.V. Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of Tractor, valid R.C. and F.C.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act by the owner of offending vehicle and also police authorities.
The petition is liable to be dismissed for want of jurisdiction as the place of accident, residence of petitioner and owner and also issuance of policy are all under Chittor District, A.P.

Apart from denying the contents of petition averments, the 1 st SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 respondent has contended that, the rider of Scooter was solely responsible for the accident and the driver of Tractor and Tailor is no way responsible for the death of deceased.
The police have filed false charge sheet against the driver of offending Tractor-Trailer by colluding with the petitioner.
The driver of offending tractor-trailer was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle at the time of accident.
Hence, there is clear breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
6. The 1st respondent has denied the age, occupation and earnings of the deceased.
It has contended that the deceased was not wearing the prescribed ISI marked helmet and not holding valid driving license to ride the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ-4070.
This is clear case of "Volunti non fit injuria".

The owner of the motor cycle was solely responsible for the death of deceased and the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ-4070.
It is contended that, the compensation claimed by the SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 petitioners is highly excessive and exaggerated.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

. On going through the said documents, it is clear that petitioners No.1 and 2 are the wives and petitioner No.3 is the son of deceased Mogilappa.

Learned counsel for petitioner has relied the judgment in MFA No7749/2016 dated 7-9-2022, in the said judgment, it is held that, the second wife and the child through second wife need to be considered as dependents.
In view of the judgment, the petitioners are the dependents.

12. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 has argued that the petitioner No.3 is the major son and he is not the dependent on the deceased.
13.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).

The Hon'ble SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 High Court of Kerala has held in this case,
the earning sons are also dependents and also entitled compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.

In the said judgment, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has relied the decision of the Apex Court reported in 2020 (11) SCC 356, (National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender) wherein it is held as under;
"para No. 48.

In a recent decision in National Insurance Company Limited v.
Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356], a claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother, the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
"12.

Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356]

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meager income between Rs. 1,00,000/and Rs.
1,50,000/per annum.

In that sense, they were largely dependent on the earning of C.Bhairamma vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185931011/

14. Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala and Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is referred in the above decision, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the major married/earning sons and married daughters are also dependents to the deceased and they are entitled for the compensation under the motor ve- hicles accident cases.
It is pertinent to note that this rela- tionship of the petitioners with the deceased was not dis- puted by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the pe- SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 titioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the de- ceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and depen- dents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.

15. ISSUE No.2 :- It is the case of the petitioners that, on 26.08.2013 at about 3.00 p.m., deceased Mogilappa was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03- AZ-4070 slowly and cautiously near Gundugallu cross, on Punganur- Appinapalle Road, Panjani, Chittoor, at that time the driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP-27-AA- 4274 and Trailer No.AP-03-UGTB-6706 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed came to wrong side and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to impact deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries in the hospital.

16. On the other hand, it is the contention of Respondent No.1 that, the rider of Scooter was solely SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 responsible for the accident and the driver of Tractor and Tailor is no way responsible for the death of deceased.
The police have filed false charge sheet against the driver of offending Tractor-Trailor by colluding with the petitioner.
Further contended that, the deceased was not wearing the prescribed ISI marked helmet and not holding valid driving license to ride the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ- 4070.
This is clear case of "Volunti non fit injuria".

The owner of the motor cycle was solely responsible for the death of deceased and the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ-4070.

Therefore, the burden is on the petitioners to prove the actionable negligence on the part of driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP-27-AA-4274 and Trailer bearing Reg.No.AP-03-UGTB-6706.
17.
In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.1 herself examined as PW.1.
She has filed affidavit in lieu of examination-in-chief and re-iterated the entire petition averments.

In order to prove this issue, she has produced SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 documents, which are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.15.
18.

20. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that, the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same"
21.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective and the evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by her.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP-27-AA-4274 and Trailor bearing Reg.No.AP-03- UGTB-6706 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.

 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Sri. C.Mogilappa caused in a Road Traffic accident.
SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 2.
The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
On 26.08.2013 at about 3.00 p.m, Sri. Mogilappa was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ-4070 slowly and cautiously on the extreme left side of the road and when he reached near Gundugallu cross, on Punganur- Appinapalle Road,
P a n j a n i , C h i t t o o r , a t t h a t t i m e t h e d r i v e r o f t h e T r a c t o r b e a r i n g Reg.No.AP-27-AA-4274 and Trailer No.AP-03-UGTB-6706 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed came to wrong side and dashed against the motor cycle.
opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to sudden death of the deceased the petitioners were deprived of love, affection, care and services of deceased.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP-27-AA-4274 and Trailer bearing Reg.No.
AP-03- UG-TB-6706 and the Panjani Police have registered the case against the driver of said Tractor-Trailer in crime No.92/2013 under Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.
The 1st respondent has admitted that, it is the insurer of offending Tractor and Trailor and contending that, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, provisions of M.V. Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of Tractor, valid R.C. and F.C.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act by the owner of offending vehicle and also police authorities.
The petition is liable to be dismissed for want of jurisdiction as the place of accident, residence of petitioner and owner and also issuance of policy are all under Chittor District, A.P.
The police have filed false charge sheet against the driver of offending Tractor-Trailer by colluding with the petitioner.
The driver of offending tractor-trailer was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle at the time of accident.
Hence, there is clear breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
It has contended that the deceased was not wearing the prescribed ISI marked helmet and not holding valid driving license to ride the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ-4070.
The owner of the motor cycle was solely responsible for the death of deceased and the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ-4070.
opennyai_summary.issue:
7. on the basis of above pleadings, the following Issues have been framed:
C.Bhairamma vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185931011/
3 ISSUES
1. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased C Mogilappa?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 26.08.2013 at about 3.00 p.m the deceased C Mogilappa was proceeding in his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ-4070,
when he reached near Gundugallu cross, on Punganur-Appinapalle road, Panjani,
Chittoor, at that time the tractor No.AP-27-AA-4274 & Trailer No.AP- 03-UGTB-6706 being drive by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and came and dashed his motor cycle, as a result he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
3. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?
If so, from which respondent?
4. What Order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.
Since the evidence led by the pe- SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 titioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the de- ceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and depen- dents of deceased.
Due to impact deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries in the hospital.
The police have filed false charge sheet against the driver of offending Tractor-Trailor by colluding with the petitioner.
Further contended that, the deceased was not wearing the prescribed ISI marked helmet and not holding valid driving license to ride the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ- 4070.
The owner of the motor cycle was solely responsible for the death of deceased and the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-AZ-4070.
Therefore, the burden is on the petitioners to prove the actionable negligence on the part of driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP-27-AA-4274 and Trailer bearing Reg.No.AP-03-UGTB-6706.
17.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective and the evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by her.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore as per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 30% of income is to be added towards future prospects.
30% of Rs.23,233/- works out to Rs.6,970/-.
1/3th of Rs.30,203/- works out to Rs.10,067/-.
, amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years under the following conventional heads.
As such, Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled to Rs.48,000/- each towards loss of consortium, Rs.18,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.18,000/- towards Funeral expenses.
. The calculation table stands as follows :-
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 31,41,216/- 2 Loss of consortium to Rs. 96,000/-
(Rs.48,000X12) 3 Loss of parental consortium Rs. 48,000/- to petitioner No.3 4 Loss of estate Rs. 18,000/-
5
Funeral expenses Rs. 18,000/-
GRAND TOTAL Rs. 33,21,216/-
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs. 33,21,216/-.
30. The Respondent No.2 is the RC owner of offending Tractor No.AP-27-AA-4274 & trailer No.AP-03-UG-6706 and Respondent No.1 is the insurer.
Hence, both the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to the SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 compensation to the Petitioner.
The primary liability is on the Respondent No.1 to pay the compensation of Rs.33,21,216/- with 6%
interest to the petitioner from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.
31. ISSUE No.4: In view of my findings on issue No.1 to 3, I proceed pass the following:
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V.Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for  compensation of Rs.33,21,216/-
 (Thirty three lakhs twenty one  thousand two hundred and  sixteen only) with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being insurer of offending tractor and SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 trailer is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two month from the date of this order.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 40 %
 Petitioner No.2 - 40 %
 Petitioner No.3 - 20 %
 After deposit of compensation  amount, release the 75% amount to  the petitioner No.1and 2 through  NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment  on proper identification and the  remaining 25% of compensation  amount shall deposited in the name  of the petitioner No.1 and 2 as  fixed deposit in any  nationalized/Scheduled bank for their choice for a period of 3 years.
However the said Petitioner No.1 and 2 are at liberty to withdraw the SCCH-26 M.V.C.No.5395/2021 periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
After deposit of compensation amount, release the entire apportionment amount to the petitioner No. 3 through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
